---
title: "How the package is checked"
---

```{r setup, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>", echo = FALSE)
```

```{r data}
read_result <- function(dir, file) {
  utils::read.csv(system.file(dir, "results", file, package = "simFastBOIN"),
                  stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
}
judgements <- c("PASS", "EXPLAINED", "FAIL", "INFO")
tally <- function(x) {
  as.numeric(table(factor(x$judgement, levels = judgements)))
}
n_of <- function(x, j) sum(x$judgement == j)
show <- function(df) knitr::kable(df, row.names = FALSE)

scripts <- data.frame(
  design = c("iBOIN", "gBOIN", "gBOIN", "Accelerated BOIN", "Waterfall",
             "Waterfall", "BOIN-ET", "TITE-BOIN-ET",
             "BOIN-ET, TITE-BOIN-ET", "BF-BOIN-ET", "BF-BOIN-ET",
             "BOIN-ETC", "BOIN-ETC", "gBOIN-ET", "gBOIN-ET",
             "TITE-gBOIN-ET", "TITE-gBOIN-ET", "BOIN12", "BOIN12",
             "TITE-BOIN12", "Comb-BOIN12, TITE-Comb-BOIN12", "U-BOIN"),
  script = c("reproduce_Zhou2021.R", "reproduce_Mu2019.R",
             "compare-with-UnifiedDoseFinding.R", "reproduce_Kojima2024.R",
             "reproduce_Zhang2016.R", "compare-waterfall-with-BOIN.R",
             "reproduce_Takeda2018.R", "reproduce_Takeda2020.R",
             "compare-with-boinet.R", "reproduce_Takeda2025.R",
             "compare-with-bfboinet.R", "reproduce_Kakizume2024.R",
             "compare-with-BOINETC.R", "reproduce_Takeda2022.R",
             "compare-with-gboinet.R", "reproduce_Takeda2023.R",
             "compare-with-tite-gboinet.R", "reproduce_Lin2020.R",
             "compare-with-escalation.R", "reproduce_Zhou2022.R",
             "reproduce_Lu2025.R", "reproduce_Zhou2019.R"),
  against = c("Zhou et al. (2021)", "Mu et al. (2019)",
              "'UnifiedDoseFinding'", "Kojima et al. (2024)",
              "Zhang and Yuan (2016)", "'BOIN'", "Takeda et al. (2018)",
              "Takeda et al. (2020)", "'boinet'", "Takeda et al. (2025)",
              "'bfboinet'", "Kakizume et al. (2024)",
              "Code of Kakizume et al. (2024)", "Takeda et al. (2022)",
              "'boinet'", "Takeda et al. (2023)", "'boinet'",
              "Lin et al. (2020)", "'escalation'", "Zhou et al. (2022)",
              "Lu et al. (2025)", "Zhou, Lee and Yuan (2019)"),
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
)
scripts$dir <- ifelse(startsWith(scripts$script, "reproduce"), "reproduce",
                      "validation")
results <- lapply(seq_len(nrow(scripts)), function(i) {
  read_result(scripts$dir[i], sub("\\.R$", ".csv", scripts$script[i]))
})
names(results) <- scripts$script

counts <- t(vapply(results, tally, numeric(4)))
colnames(counts) <- judgements
totals <- colSums(counts)

explained <- utils::read.csv(system.file("validation", "explained.csv",
                                         package = "simFastBOIN"),
                             stringsAsFactors = FALSE)

# The parts of a results file shown in the tables of judgments.
part <- list(
  "reproduce_Zhou2021.R" = function(x) {
    ifelse(startsWith(x$item, "Table"), "Table 1",
           paste0("Table S.1, ", x$design))
  },
  "reproduce_Mu2019.R" = function(x) {
    ifelse(x$item == "Table 2", "Table 2", paste0("Table 5, ", x$design))
  },
  "compare-with-UnifiedDoseFinding.R" = function(x) x$design,
  "reproduce_Kojima2024.R" = function(x) {
    paste0("Target ", sub("^target ", "", x$table), ", ", x$design)
  },
  "reproduce_Zhang2016.R" = function(x) {
    paste0(sub(",.*$", "", x$item), ", ", x$design)
  },
  "compare-waterfall-with-BOIN.R" = function(x) x$design,
  "reproduce_Takeda2018.R" = function(x) {
    ifelse(startsWith(x$item, "Scenario"), "Table 3",
           ifelse(startsWith(x$item, "Table"), "Table 2", "Boundaries"))
  },
  "reproduce_Takeda2020.R" = function(x) paste0("Table 2, ", x$design),
  "compare-with-boinet.R" = function(x) x$design,
  "reproduce_Takeda2025.R" = function(x) paste0(x$table, ", ", x$design),
  "compare-with-bfboinet.R" = function(x) x$scenario,
  "reproduce_Kakizume2024.R" = function(x) x$source,
  "compare-with-BOINETC.R" = function(x) x$source,
  "reproduce_Takeda2022.R" = function(x) {
    ifelse(startsWith(x$item, "Section"), "Boundaries",
           paste0("Table 1, ", x$design))
  },
  "compare-with-gboinet.R" = function(x) x$design,
  "reproduce_Takeda2023.R" = function(x) {
    ifelse(startsWith(x$item, "Section"), "Boundaries",
           paste0(ifelse(startsWith(x$item, "Table 1"), "Table 1",
                         "Tables S2 to S6"), ", ", x$design))
  },
  "compare-with-tite-gboinet.R" = function(x) x$design,
  "reproduce_Lin2020.R" = function(x) x$source,
  "compare-with-escalation.R" = function(x) {
    rep("Nine scenarios", nrow(x))
  },
  "reproduce_Zhou2022.R" = function(x) x$source,
  "reproduce_Lu2025.R" = function(x) x$source,
  "reproduce_Zhou2019.R" = function(x) {
    paste0(sub(",.*$", "", x$item), ", ", x$design)
  }
)

# The judgments of one results file by part.
by_part <- function(script) {
  x <- results[[script]]
  p <- part[[script]](x)
  tab <- table(factor(p, levels = unique(p)),
               factor(x$judgement, levels = judgements))
  out <- as.data.frame.matrix(tab)
  show(cbind(Part = rownames(out), out))
}

# The values of one results file that fail. The columns of the published
# or reference value, of the value of the package and of the tolerance have
# other names in the files of inst/validation/.
fails <- function(script) {
  x <- results[[script]]
  x <- x[x$judgement == "FAIL", , drop = FALSE]
  cols <- intersect(c("source", "table", "design", "scenario",
                      "configuration", "est_method", "obd_method", "item",
                      "quantity", "cell", "dose"), names(x))
  label <- do.call(paste, c(unname(as.list(x[cols])), sep = ", "))
  first <- function(cands) {
    nm <- intersect(cands, names(x))
    if (length(nm) > 0L) as.character(x[[nm[1L]]]) else rep(NA, nrow(x))
  }
  data.frame(Script = rep(script, nrow(x)), Value = label,
             Published = first(c("published", "boinet", "bfboinet",
                                 "escalation", "UnifiedDoseFinding",
                                 "BOIN")),
             Reproduced = first(c("reproduced", "simFastBOIN")),
             Tolerance = first(c("tolerance", "se")),
             stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
}

r_ <- function(script) results[[script]]
wb_settings <- nrow(unique(r_("compare-waterfall-with-BOIN.R")[
  , c("scenario", "configuration")]))
fail_in <- function(script, scenario) {
  x <- r_(script)
  c(all = n_of(x, "FAIL"),
    scenario = sum(x$judgement == "FAIL" & x$item == scenario))
}
t18 <- fail_in("reproduce_Takeda2018.R", "Scenario 11")
t20 <- fail_in("reproduce_Takeda2020.R", "Scenario 11")
```

## Four kinds of checks

Every design of the package is checked in four ways.

* **Tests.** The test suite in `tests/testthat/` checks every function on
  cases whose results are known: decision tables printed in the articles,
  limiting cases in which a design reduces to a simpler one with the same
  random numbers, and values computed beforehand by a separate
  implementation.
* **Separate implementations.** The trials of every simulation engine were
  compared, trial by trial, with an implementation of the same rules written
  in Python and fed with the random numbers of R, whose default generator
  was written again in Python for that purpose. These implementations are
  development files and are not part of the package.
* **Reference implementations.** The scripts in `inst/validation/` compare
  the package with other R packages and with the code of the authors of a
  design, exactly where the rules and the random numbers are the same and
  within simulation error otherwise.
* **Published results.** The scripts in `inst/reproduce/` compare the
  package with the tables and figures of the articles that introduced the
  designs.

This article summarizes the last two. The scripts write their judgments to
the `results/` folders of `inst/reproduce/` and `inst/validation/`, and every
number below is read from those files.

## Judgments

Every compared value receives one of four judgments.

* **PASS.** The value agrees: exactly, or to the printed digits, for a
  value that involves no random numbers, and within the tolerance stated in
  the script for a simulated value. Where the package and the reference draw
  the same trials, the values must be equal; otherwise the tolerance is a
  number of standard errors of the difference between two independent
  simulations, three or four as the script states, plus the rounding of the
  printed value.
* **EXPLAINED.** The value lies outside the tolerance for a reason that was
  found, such as a misprint in the article, or a rule of the program of the
  authors that the article does not describe. The reason is registered in
  `inst/validation/explained.csv`, which has `r nrow(explained)` rows.
* **FAIL.** The value lies outside the tolerance and no reason was found.
  These values are kept and listed below.
* **INFO.** The value is listed for information and not judged: for
  example the results of the default rules of the package where an article
  used other rules, or a quantity that an article does not describe well
  enough to be compared.

A script is run from the root of the source package after
`devtools::load_all()`. It defines its functions, and the function named in
the usage at the top of the script runs the comparison and writes the
results file, for example

```{r, echo = TRUE, eval = FALSE}
devtools::load_all()
source("inst/reproduce/reproduce_Zhou2021.R")
res <- run_reproduce_zhou2021()
table(res$design, res$judgement)
```

Some scripts take a long time, up to a few hours, and those that compare
with other packages need these packages.

## Summary

```{r summary}
summary_table <- cbind(scripts[, c("design", "script", "against")],
                       as.data.frame(counts))
names(summary_table)[1:3] <- c("Design", "Script", "Compared with")
show(summary_table)
```

Of the `r format(sum(totals[c("PASS", "EXPLAINED", "FAIL")]), big.mark = ",")`
values judged by the `r nrow(scripts)` scripts,
`r format(totals[["PASS"]], big.mark = ",")` pass,
`r totals[["EXPLAINED"]]` are explained and `r totals[["FAIL"]]` fail, and
`r format(totals[["INFO"]], big.mark = ",")` more are listed for
information. The sections below describe what each script compares.

## Designs that select the MTD

**iBOIN.** `reproduce_Zhou2021.R` compares `iboin_boundary()` with the
boundaries of Table 1 of Zhou et al. (2021), exactly, and the simulations
with the rows BOIN, iBOIN and iBOINR (the robust prior) of Table S.1 of its
supporting information, five operating characteristics in ten scenarios,
within four standard errors plus 0.05. The article does not say whether its
simulations select the MTD with or without the prior information; they are
judged with it, and the selection from the data alone is INFO.

```{r}
by_part("reproduce_Zhou2021.R")
```

**gBOIN.** `reproduce_Mu2019.R` compares the boundaries of Table 2 of Mu et
al. (2019) and the selection percentages and numbers of patients of Table 5
under the elimination rule of the article (`elim_rule = "posterior"`),
within four standard errors plus the rounding; the rule of the
'UnifiedDoseFinding' package (`elim_rule = "count"`) is INFO.
`compare-with-UnifiedDoseFinding.R` compares the same scenarios with that
package, judging the rows with its elimination rule.

```{r}
by_part("reproduce_Mu2019.R")
by_part("compare-with-UnifiedDoseFinding.R")
```

**Accelerated BOIN.** `reproduce_Kojima2024.R` compares the accelerated
BOIN design (`ABOIN` in the table, `titration_doses = 2` and
`n_earlystop = 6`) and the BOIN design with Tables 1 and 2 of Kojima et al.
(2024), within four standard errors plus the rounding. The BOIN rows of
the article agree with no early stop (`n_earlystop = 100`), although the
text states 12 patients; the rows with 12 patients and the 3+3 rows,
computed in closed form by `oc_3p3()`, are INFO.

```{r}
by_part("reproduce_Kojima2024.R")
```

**BOIN, TITE-BOIN, BF-BOIN and BE-BOIN.** `compare-with-BOIN.R` compares
`sim_boin()` with `BOIN::get.oc()` over a grid of configurations, by
equality, since the two draw the same trials for the same seed, and
`compare-with-Zhao2024.R` compares BF-BOIN with Table 4 of Zhao et al.
(2024). These scripts print their results and do not keep a results file
in the package; the tests check the agreement with the 'BOIN' package on
smaller settings. The decision tables
of TITE-BOIN are reproduced by the tests entry by entry.

## Drug combinations

**BOIN drug-combination design.** `compare-comb-with-BOIN.R` compares
`sim_comb_boin()` with `BOIN::get.oc.comb()` by equality, and
`compare-with-LinYin2017.R` sets the results beside Tables 2 and 3 of Lin
and Yin (2017), as INFO, since the package follows the 'BOIN' package where
it differs from the article. Neither keeps a results file.

**Waterfall.** `reproduce_Zhang2016.R` compares `sim_waterfall()` with
Tables IV, V and S1 of Zhang and Yuan (2016) with `boin_compatible = TRUE`,
the seed 6 and 1,000 trials, by equality with the printed digits: the
article was produced with these settings. The default rules of the package,
which keep the data of a subtrial that ends without a candidate MTD, and the
sample sizes of Table V are INFO. `compare-waterfall-with-BOIN.R` compares
every value of the output of `BOIN::get.oc.comb(mtd.contour = TRUE)` in
`r wb_settings` settings, again by equality.

```{r}
by_part("reproduce_Zhang2016.R")
by_part("compare-waterfall-with-BOIN.R")
```

## The BOIN-ET family

**BOIN-ET and TITE-BOIN-ET.** `reproduce_Takeda2018.R` compares the
boundaries and the decision tables of Table 2 of Takeda et al. (2018),
exactly, and the operating characteristics of Table 3, within four standard
errors plus 0.5 for the rounding. `reproduce_Takeda2020.R` does the same for
Table 2 of Takeda et al. (2020), whose simulations did not wait for finished
assessments (`min_completed_share = 0`). `compare-with-boinet.R` compares
`sim_boin_et()` and `sim_tite_boin_et()` with `boinet_compatible = TRUE`
with `boinet::boinet()` and `boinet::tite.boinet()`, within four standard
errors plus 0.05.

```{r}
by_part("reproduce_Takeda2018.R")
by_part("reproduce_Takeda2020.R")
by_part("compare-with-boinet.R")
```

Of the values that fail, listed at the end of this article,
`r t18[["scenario"]]` of the `r t18[["all"]]` of Takeda et al. (2018) and
`r t20[["scenario"]]` of the `r t20[["all"]]` of Takeda et al. (2020) are in
scenario 11, whose printed response rate of 0.55 at the lowest dose does not
fit the published results; the 'boinet' package too selects that dose far
more often than the article reports. In Takeda et al. (2020) the early
terminations, durations and allocations of TITE-BOIN-ET in scenarios 8, 9,
10 and 12 agree better with an exclusion of doses that uses only the
patients whose outcomes are known, which the article does not state. The
other values that fail are not explained.

**BF-BOIN-ET.** `reproduce_Takeda2025.R` compares BF-BOIN-ET-C and
BF-BOIN-ET-A with Tables 1 and 2 of Takeda et al. (2025), within four
standard errors plus 0.05, and `compare-with-bfboinet.R` compares
`sim_bf_boin_et()` with `bfboinet::get.oc.backboinet()`, within four
standard errors.

```{r}
by_part("reproduce_Takeda2025.R")
by_part("compare-with-bfboinet.R")
```

**BOIN-ETC.** `reproduce_Kakizume2024.R` compares the allocation of the
three versions of BOIN-ETC with Table 3 and Tables S1 and S4 to S9 of
Kakizume et al. (2024), within four standard errors plus the rounding, with
the rules of the code of the authors for BOIN-ETC1
(`etc1_start = "below"`, `rule4 = "authors_code"`). The selection
percentages are INFO: the code estimates the DLT rates with
`Iso::biviso()`, whose convergence decides between combinations that tie in
the exact isotonic regression of the package. `compare-with-BOINETC.R` runs
the R code of the authors with the random numbers of R after
`set.seed(1234)`, which gives the published values to the printed digits,
and judges the selection of the package on the same trials as INFO.

```{r}
by_part("reproduce_Kakizume2024.R")
by_part("compare-with-BOINETC.R")
```

**gBOIN-ET.** `reproduce_Takeda2022.R` compares the boundaries printed in
Takeda et al. (2022) and Table 1. The SAS program of the authors draws one
Bernoulli variate for every category and takes the highest that comes up,
so that the categories are not drawn with the probabilities of Table S1;
the judged rows simulate the probabilities that the program draws, with the
printed boundaries, the linear fractional polynomial, `min_obd_sample = 6`,
independent outcomes and `boinet_compatible = TRUE`, within four standard
errors plus half a unit of the printed digit. The rows with the
probabilities of Table S1 and with the default rules are INFO.
`compare-with-gboinet.R` compares `sim_gboin_et()` with
`boinet::gboinet()` under four selection rules, within four standard errors
plus 0.05.

```{r}
by_part("reproduce_Takeda2022.R")
by_part("compare-with-gboinet.R")
```

**TITE-gBOIN-ET.** `reproduce_Takeda2023.R` compares the boundaries
printed in Takeda et al. (2023) and Table 1 and Tables S2 to S6. The R
program of its supporting information, written again in C++ with the random
numbers of R, reproduces the summaries that the supporting information holds
for the program exactly. It differs from the article and from 'boinet' in
two points: where one dose has the highest mean efficacy score among the
current dose and its neighbors, it passes that dose to `sample()`, which then
draws from all doses up to it, and it excludes doses with the effective
numbers of patients. The published cells are judged with the rules of
'boinet', and those that these two points move out of the tolerance are
explained; the same simulations are also judged against the program without
the two points. `compare-with-tite-gboinet.R` compares
`sim_tite_gboin_et()` with `boinet::tite.gboinet()`, within four standard
errors plus 0.05.

```{r}
by_part("reproduce_Takeda2023.R")
by_part("compare-with-tite-gboinet.R")
```

## Utility-based designs

**BOIN12.** `reproduce_Lin2020.R` compares the desirability scores of
Table 3 of Lin et al. (2020), the boundaries of Figure 1, the example of
Section 6 of its supplement and a few values of Zhou et al. (2022), to the
printed digits, and the simulations of
Figure 3 and Figures S3 and S4 of the supplement, within three standard
errors plus 0.05, with the rules of the simulations of the article
(`tie_break = "random"`, `no_candidate = "stop"`,
`explore_from = "admissible"`); the default rules are INFO.
`compare-with-escalation.R` compares `sim_boin12()` with
`escalation::get_boin12()` in nine scenarios, within four standard errors;
the values that differ are explained by the rules of 'escalation' when a dose
becomes inadmissible.

```{r}
by_part("reproduce_Lin2020.R")
by_part("compare-with-escalation.R")
```

**TITE-BOIN12.** `reproduce_Zhou2022.R` compares the desirabilities and
estimates of Table S.3 of the supplement of Zhou et al. (2022) with
`pending_estimate = "marginal"`, to the printed digits, and the simulations
of Figure 3, within three standard errors plus half a unit of the printed
digit. The values of Equation (11) of the article and the trial durations,
whose accrual the article does not describe, are INFO.

```{r}
by_part("reproduce_Zhou2022.R")
```

**Comb-BOIN12 and TITE-Comb-BOIN12.** `reproduce_Lu2025.R` compares the
utilities of Tables 1 and 2 and Tables S2 and S3 of Lu et al. (2025) and the
tail probabilities of Figure S1, to the printed digits, and the simulations
of Figure 2, Figure S2 and Tables 3 and 4, within three standard errors plus
0.05, with `obd_bound = "contour"` and, for TITE-Comb-BOIN12,
`pending_use = "utility"`. The selection percentages of Tables 3 and 4,
which differ from those of Figure 2 for the same trials, and the durations
are INFO. The values that fail are bars of TITE-Comb-BOIN12, whose accrual
and waiting rules the article does not describe, and selection percentages
of Comb-BOIN12, for a reason that was not found.

```{r}
by_part("reproduce_Lu2025.R")
```

**U-BOIN.** There is no reference implementation. `reproduce_Zhou2019.R`
compares the boundaries of Table 2 and Table S2 of Zhou, Lee and Yuan
(2019), the utility tables S4 to S6 of its supporting information and the
true utilities, to the printed digits, and the simulations of Table 3 and
Tables S8 and S9, within four standard errors plus half a unit of the
printed digit, with the rates of Scenario 7 of Table S8 for Scenario 7 of
Table 3 and with s1 = 12 for Table S8, with which the published results
agree. The admissibility of Tables S4 to S6 is judged with the default prior
and with `prior_resp = c(0.05, 0.05)`, which reproduces it, and the
simulations with the printed rates and with the s1 = 9 of the text are
judged as well.

```{r}
by_part("reproduce_Zhou2019.R")
```

## Values that are explained

The rows of `inst/validation/explained.csv`, grouped by script and reason.

```{r explained}
ex <- stats::aggregate(item ~ file + reason, data = explained, FUN = length)
ex <- ex[order(match(ex$file, scripts$script), -ex$item), ]
names(ex) <- c("Script", "Reason", "Values")
show(ex[, c("Script", "Values", "Reason")])
```

## Values that fail

```{r fails}
fail_table <- do.call(rbind, lapply(scripts$script, fails))
```

The `r nrow(fail_table)` values that fail, by script. For Kojima et al.
(2024), Mu et al. (2019), Takeda et al. (2022) and Zhou et al. (2022) no
reason was found; for Takeda et al. (2018) and (2020) and Lu et al. (2025)
the sections above describe them.

```{r}
show(fail_table)
```
